one_line: Let the child hold the box to the lens, show the game on a table, end on a one-number verdict.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 handheld in a kitchen: a girl about 9 to 11 lifts a game box out of brown wrapping; at 0:01 she holds it to the lens, smiling. Voiceover (transcript): "קיבלנו מקודקוד את תעלומה בגינה". No text.
q1_hook.why: A child opening a parcel and showing the box to the camera is a real, lively moment, with the product handled from 0:00 (H8, S1, K8), and the stolen-vegetables premise is a small mystery (H5). But there is no text, and the first words are "we received", not a benefit (H1, H2, H6).

beats.what: Girl lifts the box out of wrapping and holds it up to the camera
Hands take tiles from the box tray and lay out a grid of garden and clock cards
A suspect card held up (a mole with a pumpkin); red markers on a green garden board
Tiles are crossed out with red X marks; hands move cards; "לפסול את החשודים" (transcript)
beats.why: Elimination, the core of the game

beats.what: A mole with a carrot card is held up to the lens and laid on the table
Close-up of the box title, age 6+, and the Kodkod logo
beats.why: A clear brand and age shot

beats.what: The girl hides half her face behind the box; sticker "מדד אבוק: ציון 9"
beats.why: A one-number verdict and a smile

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None asked. Caption: "משחק קופסה שבו הילדים צריכים לשתף פעולה במקום לריב מי ניצח?" is a rhetorical question, not a prompt, and a gift or family-time idea parents could send, but it names no person.
q2_flow.why: The mystery premise is opened at 0:00 and the suspect is revealed at 0:24, a story with a payoff (H5, K2). The 0:14 to 0:23 stretch is hands-only crossing out with no text to explain it, which is hard to follow (R3). The verdict comes in the last 2 s (R4).

q3_cta.what: None in the video: no spoken ask, no text ask, no link or code. The last frames carry the rating sticker "מדד אבוק: ציון 9". The caption has no ask, only a checklist and the tag @mykodkod.
q3_cta.why: A parent who likes it has no next step, no shop, no link, no where to buy (C6). One action would help, but nothing asks for it (C1, C5). The sell is very light, brand time short, and the benefits are stated in the caption (C7).

q4_shown.what: The box lifted from wrapping 0:00; tiles from the tray 0:03; a laid-out grid 0:05; a suspect card 0:07; red markers 0:11; tiles crossed out with red X marks 0:14-0:28; the box title and logo 0:29; the girl behind the box 0:33. No price.
q4_shown.why: The game is handled from 0:00 and the play is shown in full on a table (S1, S4). A child reviewer is first-hand (S6). The girl's face and a rating sticker are the personality (K8). A rating sticker as a verdict is not backed by any listed principle. No price (S3).

q5_edit.what: 9 shots in 34.6 s, about 3.8 s each; hard cuts, mostly handheld, with two long gameplay shots of 4.7 s and 11.2 s. No speed changes. Voiceover throughout, no subtitles. One sticker at 0:33. Ends on the girl behind the box.
q5_edit.why: Motion and a cut within 3 s open it (E1), and the pace is moderate (E2). The speech carries all the meaning with no text, so it fails muted (E4). It ends on the verdict (E8).

q6_topic.what: A child's review of a cooperative detective board game, with a rating. Serves parents looking for a screen-free family game.
q6_topic.why: "Instead of arguing about who won" (transcript) speaks to a real family concern (K6), and the caption's checklist gives practical reasons (K4). A child's own verdict is something a parent can send to another parent (R5).

q7_filmed.what: Handheld phone throughout. A kitchen at night in warm artificial light for the girl; a high-angle shot over a glass-topped wooden table for the play, with reflections of the lamp on the glass. Close-ups of the box.
q7_filmed.why: A real kitchen and a home table look native (H8, F7), but lamp glare and hand shake in the table shots make some cards hard to read (F7). The box fills the frame in the close-ups (F4), and the tiles are seen from above, as the viewer would (F5).

q8_text.on_screen: No text over the speech anywhere. A sticker in the lower middle of the frame at 0:33-0:34: a cartoon of a bearded man giving a thumbs up and the words "מדד אבוק: ציון 9". The game name "תעלומה בגינה" and "משחק שיתופי לצוות בלשים צעירים" appear only on the box.
q8_text.caption: "משחק קופסה שבו הילדים צריכים לשתף פעולה במקום לריב מי ניצח?". About 90 words: a question, a short review, a four-item checklist, a joke line, the disclosure "המשחק התקבל מקודקוד לצורך סקירה", the tag @mykodkod. No hashtags.
q8_text.why: With no burned-in text, a muted viewer gets only the pictures (T1, T3), and the sticker sits in the bottom 35% over the box (T4). The caption's first line is a question with the product idea, and a checklist (T7). The disclosure is in words but at the end, below "more" (T8).

weak_points: No subtitles or text; 11 s of hands-only crossing out, hard to follow; no CTA or place to buy; disclosure only at the end of the caption; lamp glare; the girl's face with her name in the caption.
lumebook_takeaway: Film a gifted-book review in three phone shots: a child opening the parcel, top-down pages on a table, and the cover close-up with a rating sticker and subtitles.
not_verified: Whose voice it is, the girl's or an adult's. Whether the girl is the account owner's child. The transcript words ("החפרפרד", "העירקות") look misheard, so only the clear opening is quoted. Price. Music is not evident. Whether the sticker is a recurring format of the account (the caption names no series). Lead edit 18 Oct: resolution remarks removed, because the downloaded copy can be smaller than what was posted.
